question: Do backed pairs (P1, P1+) and live junctions never meeting (P2) hold at every reached census stage, are reached open meet-once tables rigid, and does any other-states collision among legal meet-once arrangements of at most 7 junctions have both sides backed or peeling to depth 1 or 2?

definitions.P1: every two junctions a live junction meets also meet a junction other than it
definitions.P1+: that junction holds no loose distinction
definitions.depth: successive peels (remove live junctions) at which P1+ and P2 hold
definitions.Q: P1 required of closed junctions instead

public_inputs.run: scripts/longrun.py launch census_job.py --out runs/parent-census; scripts/longrun.py launch static_job.py --out runs/parent-static (8 workers, 16G cap each); .venv/bin/python -B static_pairs.py runs/parent-static
public_inputs.reused: CENSUS-READ-20261118-001A job.py and exact_table_v2.py; networkx graph atlas

forbidden_inputs: Changing C1, C2, R1, S0, S1a-S1c after the runs
cheapest_meaningful_control: S0: the known pop-0308 pair found as other states; Q as a matched control property

predictions.S0: other-states collisions exist, pop-0308 among them
predictions.S1a: no other-states pair both backed (P1) in the backed stratum
